messages.subject: Generating an estimate of expected cluster size given tremendous
parts:
Hello All,

My name is Brendan Shirkey and I am graduate student trying to develop aeri=
al survey protocols for diving ducks using distance sampling techniques. W=
e have what I believe is a relatively unique problem in that we are dealing=
with a clustered population (flocks of diving ducks) but these clusters ra=
nge in size from 1 individual to 20 or 30 thousand individuals. We are ple=
ased with the performance of the detection model; however we are bit torn w=
ith how to determine expected flock size. Currently, we are using the opti=
on in distance that takes the regression of the ln of flock size against g(=
x) in order to account for the increased detection probability of larger gr=
oups. We have also tried including flock size as a covariate, but I don=92=
t even know if this is appropriate given the tremendous range in flock size=
. If anyone has dealt with a similar problem in distance their insight wou=
ld be much appreciated. Specifically, we are wondering if anyone has any t=
houghts on what might be the most statistically valid way of estimating exp=
ected flock size in Distance given the tremendous variance we are dealing w=
ith. Any suggestions or discussion would be much appreciated.

Brendan Shirkey
Graduate student at Michigan State University
shir...@osu.edu
